name: Heat maps
summary: Shaded matrices that show where to look: capability and application portfolios, risk grids, capacity by week, heat-tile maps, readiness and survey results.

templates.name: Capability heat map, six sites
templates.purpose: Compare capability maturity across every site on one dense grid, with a five-step legend.

slide.title: Maturity falls away from the main campus toward Harbor

templates.name: Capability heat map, takeaway rail
templates.purpose: A four-site heat map on the left and three headline takeaways on a right panel.

slide.title: Harbor trails on every capability

body.text: capabilities sit at level 2 or below at Harbor.
is the six-site average for care coordination, the weakest row.
is the six-site average for revenue cycle, the pattern to replicate.

templates.name: Capability gap heat map, three numbered callouts
templates.purpose: A gap heat map with three numbered badges on hot cells, keyed to short explanations on the right.

slide.title: Three gaps drive most of the distance to target

items.title: Care coordination at Harbor
items.text: No shared care plan or referral tracking; clinics hand off by phone and fax.

items.title: Scheduling at Harbor
items.text: Templates differ by clinic, so open slots never reach the central call center.

items.title: Data and analytics at Ridgeview
items.text: Reports are built by hand each month and cannot be compared with other sites.

templates.name: Capability heat map, narrative split
templates.purpose: A tall heat map in the wide column with a short narrative beside the title.

slide.title: Strong at the core, thin at the edges

items.text: Revenue cycle and documentation reach level 3 or better at the main campus.
Only the main campus holds a level 3 or 4 in more than half the rows.
Harbor has no capability above level 2, and two sit at level 0.

templates.name: Capability heat map, nav rail
templates.purpose: A seven-row heat map with subtitled row headers and an average column, under a section nav rail.

slide.title: Care coordination is the weakest row overall

templates.name: Capability gap heat map, annotated
templates.purpose: A gap heat map with a hand-drawn underscore on the worst row and a straight arrow to a callout card.

slide.title: One row carries the largest gap to target

body.p: Referral status lives in faxes and phone notes, so no one sees a patient's whole path.

items: Nine other cells sit in the large band, all at Ridgeview or Harbor.
Main campus has no gap above moderate.

templates.name: Application portfolio heat map
templates.purpose: Score each application on fit, cost, risk and debt, and tag a disposition in the last column.

slide.title: Nine applications, four dispositions

templates.name: Application portfolio heat map, disposition panel
templates.purpose: A nine-row portfolio heat map beside a right panel that counts every application by disposition.

slide.title: Fourteen of 30 apps leave or move

body.text: Retiring seven apps removes $3.2M of annual run cost.

templates.name: Application portfolio heat map, grouped by domain
templates.purpose: Applications grouped under domain header rows, with fit and exposure legends below.

slide.title: Revenue cycle holds the most exposure per application

templates.name: Risk heat map, keyed risk list
templates.purpose: A five-by-five likelihood and impact grid in the tall column, with risk IDs in cells and a keyed list beside the title.

slide.title: Three risks sit in the top two bands

templates.name: Risk heat map, before and after mitigation
templates.purpose: Two smaller five-by-five grids side by side, with the same risk IDs moving down after mitigation.

slide.title: Mitigation clears the top two bands of the grid

templates.name: Risk heat map, annotated hot cell
templates.purpose: A five-by-five grid with a hand-drawn circle on the hottest cell and a straight arrow to a callout card.

slide.title: One risk is both certain and critical

body.p: Owner: CIO. Mitigation: dual-run the lab and pharmacy interfaces for two weeks.

items: R10 and R3 follow at scores of 20 and 16.
Both share the same migration team and cutover window.
After the dual run, R1 drops to a score of 15.

templates.name: Capacity heat map, roles by week
templates.purpose: Roles by week shaded by load against capacity, with a callout strip for the over-allocated weeks.

slide.title: Weeks 4 to 7 overload two roles

body.p: The integration architect runs over 100% from week 4 to week 7, and the data engineer joins in weeks 5 and 6.

templates.name: Capacity heat map, sprint by sprint
templates.purpose: Teams by sprint shaded by committed story points, with a capacity column and three reading cards.

slide.title: Sprints 4 to 6 carry the heaviest commitments

body.p: Every team commits above 24 points while go-live prep peaks.
Commits above its 36-point capacity in sprints 4 to 6.
Load eases to 26 points or fewer everywhere before the freeze.

templates.name: Heat-tile capability map, six domains
templates.purpose: Six domain columns of capability tiles filled by investment priority on a five-step heat scale, with a legend.

slide.title: Denials, master data and self-scheduling top the list

templates.name: Heat-tile capability map, insight cards
templates.purpose: Four domain columns of heat tiles on the left and three insight cards on the right.

slide.title: Four domains set the investment order

body.p: Both sit at the top and feed each other: bad data drives denials.
Highest access need and the lowest build effort in the map.
Already working; revisit after the revenue cycle program.

templates.name: Readiness heat map, narrative column
templates.purpose: Stakeholder groups by change dimension on a gap scale, with three short narrative blocks beside it.

slide.title: Skills and sustainment are the widest readiness gaps

body.label: Widest gaps
body.title: Physicians and nurses
body.body: Both groups score 3 on buy-in or skills, the two levers that decide adoption.

body.label: Sustainment
body.title: No group is secure
body.body: Six of seven groups carry a gap of 2 or more once the team steps back.

body.label: Strength
body.title: Leaders and IT
body.body: Executives and the service desk are ready to coach others.

templates.name: Readiness heat map, site split
templates.purpose: A tall site-by-dimension heat map on the left with the title and a short narrative on the right.

slide.title: Harbor Clinics are the least ready site

items.text: The only site with a critical gap, on tools, and a large gap on buy-in.
Urgent care staff cannot spare time for training.
No gap above small; use its super users to coach the others.

templates.name: Compact heat map, takeaway left
templates.purpose: A small five-by-four matrix beside a left panel that holds the takeaway in large type.

slide.title: Recovery is the weakest control

body.text: Four of five clinical systems have never tested a recovery.
Backups exist; the untested failover is the exposure.

items: Test failover for the imaging archive and the EHR before go-live.
Document recovery steps for the imaging archive, which scores worst on every control.

templates.name: Compact heat map, takeaway right
templates.purpose: A small five-by-four matrix with two notes beneath, and a right panel with the headline number.

slide.title: Inventory is the weakest data domain

body.label: Strongest
body.title: Orders and roster
body.body: Both clear a good score on three of four checks.

body.label: Weakest
body.title: Inventory
body.body: Timely data scores one; counts lag the shelf by days.

body.text: of patient records pass all four checks.

templates.name: Survey heat map, scores by group
templates.purpose: Survey statements by respondent group, shaded with the lowest scores hottest and the average printed in each cell.

slide.title: Time savings and workflow fit score lowest

templates.name: Survey heat map, split with narrative
templates.purpose: A tall survey heat map in the wide column, with the finding and three short points beside the title.

slide.title: Clinicians rate the new system lowest

source.text: Northfield go-live pulse survey, n = 412, Sep 2026.

rows.c0: I have the training I need
I know who to ask for help
Data in the system is trusted
I would recommend it to a peer
Alerts help more than they interrupt

items.text: Physicians and nurses rate time savings, workflow fit and alerts lowest.
Their scores run well above those of the people doing the work.
Fix alert noise and order-set layout first; both are configuration, not build.
